items.title: (Updated) Microsoft Purview: Archive SharePoint files under retention policies
items.body:
Updated November 23, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.
[What and why]
Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management now allows admins to archive SharePoint files based on retention policies. This helps organizations reduce storage costs by moving inactive content to Microsoft 365 Archive while maintaining compliance and discoverability. Archived content is excluded from Copilot indexing, which can improve the relevance of Copilot responses by focusing results on current, active data.
[Rollout schedule]
General Availability (GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in mid-January 2027 (previously early December 2026) and expected to complete by mid-February 2027 (previously early January)
[Impact on your organization]
Who is affected
• Admins managing Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management
• Organizations using retention policies in SharePoint Online and OneDrive
Platforms and services
• Microsoft Purview (Data Lifecycle Management)
• SharePoint Online
• OneDrive
• Microsoft 365 Archive
• Microsoft Copilot
What will happen
• A new Archive option will be available within retention policy settings in Data Lifecycle Management.
• Admins can configure retention policies to move inactive files to Microsoft 365 Archive storage.
• Archived files remain available for compliance scenarios, including eDiscovery.
• Archived content will be excluded from Copilot indexing, helping improve answer relevance.
• This feature is not enabled by default and requires admin configuration.
• Existing retention policies and compliance configurations remain unchanged unless updated by admins.
[Action required and recommendations]
No immediate action is required. To prepare for and take advantage of this feature, we recommend that you:
• Review your current retention policies in Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management.
• Evaluate opportunities to reduce storage costs by archiving inactive content.
• Update retention policies to include the new Archive option where appropriate.
• Inform compliance and records management stakeholders about this new capability.
• Review internal documentation and processes related to data lifecycle and storage optimization.
Learn more: Configure Microsoft 365 retention settings to automatically retain or delete content | Microsoft Learn
[Compliance considerations]
QuestionAnswerDoes the change store new customer data, and if so where, is it cached or permanently stored?Files moved by retention policies are relocated to Microsoft 365 Archive storage, a distinct storage tier, and are stored there until restored or otherwise actioned.Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Archived files move out of active storage into Microsoft 365 Archive, changing how those files are stored and accessed going forward.Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Archived content is excluded from Copilot indexing, which changes what data Copilot can access and surface in responses.Does the change modify, interrupt, or disable Purview capabilities such as retention policies, holds, or eDiscovery?Retention policies gain a new archive action, and archived files remain subject to eDiscovery, extending existing retention and discovery workflows.

items.title: Microsoft Teams: Tenant policy controls who can record and transcribe
items.body:
[What and Why:]
Teams administrators can use a policy to configure who may start recording and transcription. The policy supports two participant scopes: organizers and co-organizers, or organizers, co-organizers, and presenters. For each scope, administrators can specify whether meeting organizers can or cannot change the setting.
This provides a centrally managed default or enforced restriction for meetings organized by users assigned the policy, reducing the need for per-meeting configuration.
[Rollout Schedule:]
Targeted Release (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by mid-December 2026.
General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in late December 2026 and expect to complete by late December 2026.
General Availability (GCC): We will begin rolling out in late December 2026 and expect to complete by late January 2027.
General Availability (GCC High): We will begin rolling out in mid-February 2027 and expect to complete by late February 2027.
General Availability (DoD): We will begin rolling out in mid-February 2027 and expect to complete by early March 2027.
[Impact on Your Organization:]
A new Who can record and transcribe policy control will be available in the Recording & transcription section of the applicable Teams meeting policy in the Teams admin center.
The default value is Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters. Organizers can change, which preserves the current behavior.
Administrators can select one of the following four options in a single dropdown:
Who can record and transcribe - policy optionBehaviorOrganizers and co-organizers. Organizers can changeDefaults to organizers and co-organizers. Organizers can also allow presenters through the existing meeting option.Organizers and co-organizers. Organizers can't changeLocks the policy value. Presenters and attendees cannot start recording or transcription.Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters. Organizers can changeDefaults to organizers, co-organizers, and presenters. Organizers can restrict the roles through the existing meeting option.Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters. Organizers can't changeLocks the policy value. The organizer cannot change the role selection.These configurations remain subject to existing recording and transcription availability controls and any sensitivity label that configures this option.
• Enforcement: When organizer changes are blocked, Meeting options shows the policy value as read-only with a notice that it is locked by meeting policy. The effective role restriction is also enforced when a participant tries to start recording or transcription.
• Sensitivity labels and templates: A sensitivity label that configures this option takes precedence over the meeting policy. A locked meeting policy takes precedence over a meeting template. An unlocked policy supplies a default.
• Related meeting options: The existing Who can record and transcribe meeting option remains a Teams Premium or Microsoft 365 Copilot feature.
[Action Required/Recommendations:]
• No action is required. If you do not configure the new policy, existing recording and transcription behavior remains unchanged.
• If your organization needs to prevent presenters from starting recording or transcription, consider using the new Who can record and transcribe policy.
• Review policy assignments, sensitivity labels, and meeting templates to confirm the effective behavior.
• Notify meeting organizers and helpdesk teams of any changes and update internal guidance.
[Compliance considerations:]
No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

items.title: Microsoft SharePoint: Agent Chat web part to bring Copilot agents into SharePoint pages
items.body:
[What and Why:]
We're introducing the Agent Chat web part in SharePoint, allowing organizations to embed their existing Microsoft 365 Copilot agents directly into SharePoint pages. This helps organizations make agents easier to discover and use by bringing conversational AI into familiar intranet experiences, alongside relevant information, instructions, and resources.
[Rollout Schedule:]
Public Preview (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-November 2026 and expect to complete by late January 2027.
General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-January 2027 and expect to complete by late March 2027.
General Availability (GCC): We will begin rolling out in mid-January 2027 and expect to complete by late March 2027.
General Availability (GCC High): We will begin rolling out in mid-January 2027 and expect to complete by late March 2027.
General Availability (DoD): We will begin rolling out in mid-January 2027 and expect to complete by late March 2027.
[Impact on Your Organization:]
Who is affected: SharePoint page authors who want to embed Copilot agents. Users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and access to the configured agent.
Platforms/Services: SharePoint Online, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft Copilot Studio.
What will happen: SharePoint page authors can add the Agent Chat web part to pages using the standard page editing experience. Authors can select published agents already available to them in Microsoft 365 Copilot. Users can interact with agents directly from SharePoint pages and continue conversations in a full-screen chat experience. Organizations can place agents alongside relevant SharePoint content to help users discover and engage with them. Existing SharePoint page permissions and agent access permissions remain independent. Adding an agent to a page does not automatically grant users access to that agent. SharePoint page content is not automatically passed to the agent.
[Action Required/Recommendations:]
No admin action is required before rollout. The Agent Chat web part becomes available as part of the rollout.We recommend informing SharePoint page authors and support teams about this capability and reviewing the documentation: Use Agent Chat web part in SharePoint.
[Compliance considerations:]
No compliance impact is expected for this change. SharePoint does not store Copilot agent chat data or change how agent data is processed.

items.title: Use Copilot to explain selected slide content in PowerPoint Live
items.body:
[What and Why:]
Copilot in PowerPoint Live helps meeting attendees understand presentation content while it's being shared. Attendees can select a word, phrase or acronym on a slide and get a quick explanation from Copilot, based on the context of the presentation. This feature is already available worldwide and is now coming to GCC, GCC High and DoD.
[Rollout Schedule:]
General Availability (GCC, GCC High, DoD): We will begin rolling out on mid November 2026 and expect to complete by mid November 2026.
[Impact on Your Organization:]
Attendees in a PowerPoint Live session can use Copilot to get explanations of unfamiliar terms, acronyms or concepts without leaving the presentation. Explanations are based on what's on the slide, so attendees can stay engaged and follow along without interrupting the presenter.
How it works:
• During a PowerPoint Live session, select the Copilot feature from the toolbar at the bottom of the screen.
• Select a word or phrase on the slide (for example, an acronym).
• Select Explain this.
• Copilot opens the chat pane with an explanation of the selected content.
This feature is on by default.
[Action Required/Recommendations:]
No admin action is required. You may want to let your users know about this new capability and update any internal training or documentation as needed.
[Compliance considerations:]
No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

items.title: (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot: new guided Copilot onboarding experience
items.body:
Updated November 18, 2026: We have updated this post as a reminder. Thank you for your patience.
[What and why]
To help organizations increase Microsoft 365 Copilot adoption and build user confidence, we are introducing a new admin-led Copilot onboarding experience for Frontier participants. This guided, in-product experience helps users learn how to use Copilot through role-based activities within the Copilot app. The experience is tailored to the user’s familiarity with Copilot and their license assignment, helping users build confidence through relevant, guided examples while giving organizations control over how onboarding is introduced. This supports Personal and Team Productivity by helping users learn how to use Copilot effectively in their daily work.
[Rollout schedule]
• Frontier (Worldwide): Rollout begins in late October 2026 and is expected to complete by late November 2026 (previously early November).
[Impact on your organization]
Who is affected
• Microsoft 365 admins participating in the Frontier program who want to provide guided Copilot onboarding to their users.
• Users for whom the onboarding experience has been enabled and shared.
Platforms and services
• Microsoft 365 admin center
• Microsoft 365 Copilot
• Learning Agent
• Viva Learning (reporting)
What will happen
• This is a new, optional onboarding experience that does not change, replace, or retire existing Microsoft 365 Copilot functionality.
• The experience is disabled by default and must be enabled by an admin with the Global Administrator, Knowledge Administrator, or AI Administrator role. Admins can enable the experience in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot settings > Microsoft 365 Copilot onboarding and include their organization's AI policy as part of the onboarding experience.
• After enabling onboarding, admins can share the experience with users by using the provided email template or onboarding deep link. When users open the onboarding deep link, the Copilot app launches in the preferred destination set by the admin that shared the experience, such as the Copilot app for Windows, Copilot on the web, or Copilot in Teams.
• Learning Agent automatically starts the onboarding experience, which takes approximately 5 to 10 minutes to complete, and is personalized based on the user's role, work context, familiarity with Copilot, and license assignment.
• The Starter journey collects information from the user to personalize the onboarding experience.
• The Premium journey uses available work and role context to provide relevant examples of how the user can apply Copilot to their work. This journey is only available to users with a Copilot Premium license.
• If desired, admins with the Global Administrator or Knowledge Administrator role can access and use Viva Learning reporting to review onboarding completion.
Starter journey Copilot onboarding experience
Premium journey Copilot onboarding experience
Microsoft 365 admin center Copilot onboarding flyout menu
[Action required and recommendations]
No action is required unless you want to enable Microsoft 365 Copilot onboarding for your organization during the Frontier rollout. If you plan to use the experience:
• Ensure Learning Agent and Microsoft 365 Copilot are enabled for targeted users who will participate in the onboarding experience.
• In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot settings > Microsoft 365 Copilot onboarding and enable the experience.
• Review your organization's AI policy and determine whether you want to include it in the onboarding experience.
• Share the onboarding experience with users by using the provided email template or onboarding deep link. We recommend that you share the onboarding experience with new or inexperienced users to help them learn how to use Copilot in their role.
• If you want to view reporting and have the Global Administrator or Knowledge Administrator role, use Viva Learning reporting to review onboarding completion.
[Learn more]
We will update this post with new documentation.
[Compliance considerations]
No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

items.title: Microsoft SharePoint: Enhanced data access governance reports and site access reviews
items.body:
[What and why]
Microsoft SharePoint is enhancing data access governance reports and site access reviews to give SharePoint admins more control, flexibility, and transparency when identifying and addressing potential data exposure. These updates help admins prioritize sites that may present the greatest data risk, direct review requests to the appropriate recipients, and track whether notifications were delivered.
[Rollout schedule]
• General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, and DoD): We will begin rolling out in late November 2026 and expect to complete by early December 2026
[Impact on your organization]
Who is affected
• SharePoint admins who use data access governance reports and initiate site access reviews
Platforms and services
• SharePoint Online
• SharePoint admin center
• Data access governance reports
• Site access reviews
What will happen
• The Site permissions across your organization report will show the number of files flagged by sensitive information types, such as credit card numbers, Social Security numbers, and custom-defined patterns.
• SharePoint admins will be able to use this information to prioritize sites that may present greater data risk.
• Admins will be able to direct site access review requests to site owners or site admins.
• Admins will be able to send either one consolidated review email to all recipients or separate emails to individual recipients.
• Admins will be able to view email delivery status and the complete recipient list for review requests.
[Action required and recommendations]
No action is required before rollout. We recommend that SharePoint admins:
• Review current site permissions and data access governance processes.
• Inform relevant SharePoint admins about the enhanced reporting and site access review capabilities.
• Update internal documentation and workflows as appropriate.
• Confirm that site owners and site admins are prepared to receive and complete site access review requests.
Learn more
• Data access governance reports for SharePoint sites - SharePoint in Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn
• Initiate site access reviews for Data access governance reports - SharePoint in Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn
[Compliance considerations]
ConsiderationExplanationDoes the change alter how existing customer data is accessed or processed?Yes. The Site permissions across your organization report will display counts of files flagged by sensitive information types. Does the change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities?Yes. SharePoint admins will receive additional reporting information about files flagged by sensitive information types and greater visibility into site access review recipients and email delivery status.Does the change include an admin control?Yes. SharePoint admins will be able to select review recipients and choose between consolidated and individual review emails.

items.title: (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot: Copilot Pages and Notebooks Creation in OneDrive
items.body:
Updated November 16, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.
[What and why]
We're changing where newly created Copilot Pages are stored. Going forward, Copilot Pages created in Copilot Chat, the Microsoft 365 Copilot app, and new Copilot Notebooks will be stored in OneDrive for Business instead of their current location.
This change enables organizations to manage newly created Copilot Pages using existing OneDrive for Business governance, compliance, data protection, retention, and lifecycle management capabilities.
[Rollout schedule]
• General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-October 2026 (previously mid-August) and expected to complete by mid-December 2026 (previously late November)
• General Availability (GCC, GCC High, and DoD): Beginning in mid-November 2026 (previously mid-September) and expected to complete by mid-December 2026 (previously early December)
[Impact on your organization]
Who is affected
Users who create Copilot Pages in:
• Copilot Chat
• Microsoft 365 Copilot app
• Copilot Notebooks
Microsoft 365 administrators responsible for governance, compliance, retention, and content management
Platforms and services
• Microsoft 365 Copilot
• Copilot Chat
• Copilot Notebooks
• OneDrive for Business
• Microsoft Purview compliance solutions
What will happen
After rollout:
• Newly created Copilot Pages will be stored in users' OneDrive for Business.
• New Copilot Pages will appear alongside other OneDrive files, such as Word, Excel, and PowerPoint documents.
• New Copilot Notebooks and artifacts created within them will appear alongside other OneDrive files, such as Word, Excel, and PowerPoint documents.
• Existing OneDrive governance, compliance, data protection, retention, lifecycle management, reporting, and investigation capabilities will apply to newly created Copilot Pages.
In addition to all existing governance and management capabilities, the following additional OneDrive for Business capabilities will apply to newly created Copilot Pages:
Compliance and legal
• Standard file path-based eDiscovery
• Retention labels with record locking
• Information Barriers
• Compliance Boundaries
Data protection
• Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies and mitigation workflows
• Third-party governance solutions that support OneDrive content
Lifecycle management
• Retention and lifecycle policies
• Existing departed-user workflows for OneDrive content
Monitoring and oversight
• OneDrive storage reporting
• Administrative investigations of content stored in OneDrive
Unaffected files
• Existing Copilot Pages will remain in their current location and will not be migrated as part of this change.
• Existing Copilot Notebooks will continue to store all newly created pages in SharePoint Embedded. Only Copilot Notebooks created after this change will store pages in OneDrive.
• Loop workspaces are not affected and will continue to use their current storage location.
IT Admin controls
• If your organization has set Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks to Disabled, that setting will continue to be honored after this change.
• This admin control is planned for future retirement. Microsoft will provide additional communication and transition guidance before the setting is retired.
[Action required and recommendations]
No action is required for the rollout.
We recommend that administrators:
• Review existing DLP, retention, and compliance policies that apply to OneDrive for Business.
• Verify that any third-party governance or eDiscovery solutions are configured to monitor OneDrive content as appropriate.
• Update internal documentation and governance guidance for AI-generated content.
• Communicate to users that newly created Copilot Pages will be stored in their OneDrive for Business.
[Compliance considerations]
QuestionAnswerDoes this change alter where customer data is stored?Yes. Newly created Copilot Pages will be stored in OneDrive for Business instead of their previous storage location.Does this change affect compliance and governance capabilities?Yes. Newly created Copilot Pages will be subject to OneDrive for Business compliance capabilities, including eDiscovery, retention labels with record locking, Information Barriers, and Compliance Boundaries.Does this change affect data protection controls?Yes. Existing OneDrive for Business data protection controls, including Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies and supported third-party governance solutions, can be applied to newly created Copilot Pages.Does this change affect lifecycle management and retention processes?Yes. Existing OneDrive for Business retention policies, lifecycle management capabilities, and departed-user workflows will apply to newly created Copilot Pages.Does this change affect how administrators monitor or investigate content?Yes. Administrators will be able to use standard OneDrive for Business reporting, monitoring, and investigation capabilities for newly created Copilot Pages.

items.title: Release Planner Retirement: D365, Power Platform, and Dataverse Move to AI at Work
items.body:
Release Planner is now retired. To stay informed about upcoming capabilities and prepare your organization for feature rollout and adoption, use the resources shared below. To view product availability for Dynamics 365, Power Platform and Copilot Studio, visit the new Learn page at https://aka.ms/d365-product-availability.
Starting this fall, Dynamics 365, Power Platform, and Dataverse roadmap content is joining the
AI at Work roadmap, giving customers a single destination
to discover upcoming capabilities, track rollout progress, and plan adoption across Microsoft's
business applications, productivity, and AI portfolio.
As part of this transition, Release Planner will
retire on November 15, 2026. Microsoft is also retiring the twice-yearly release wave communication
model in favor of continuous roadmap disclosure and change communications. New capabilities will be
published to the AI at Work roadmap as they become committed and ready to share, providing a more
current and comprehensive view of upcoming innovation.
When this will happen
• September 2026: New Dynamics 365, Power Platform, and Dataverse roadmap items begin publishing directly to the AI at Work roadmap.
• Fall 2026: Existing roadmap items with Public Preview or General Availability dates on or after June 1, 2026 transition from Release Planner to the AI at Work roadmap.
• By November 15, 2026: Release Planner retires. The AI at Work roadmap becomes Microsoft's primary destination for public roadmap information.
How this affects your organization
If your organization uses Release Planner,
Release Plans on Microsoft Learn,
or release wave announcements for roadmap planning, you will need to transition to the AI at Work roadmap.
Key changes include:
• Release Planner will retire on November 15, 2026.
•
New Release Plans will no longer be published on
Microsoft Learn beginning
in September 2026. Existing Release Plans will remain available for historical reference.
• The September 2026 Release Wave 2 announcement will not occur because release wave communications are being retired.
• Roadmap information will be published continuously rather than grouped into twice-yearly release wave announcements.
•
Roadmap content will be available
through filtering, CSV export, RSS subscriptions,
and the
Release Communications MCP Server
pulls roadmap information directly into your own AI tools and workflows.
• Personalized saved views from My Release Plans will not migrate to the AI at Work roadmap.
What is not changing
This transition changes how Microsoft communicates roadmap information. It does not change how products are built, released, or deployed.
The following remain unchanged:
• Product release schedules
• Deployment and rollout processes
• Upgrade planning and support lifecycles
• Preview and testing programs
• Message Center notifications, which remain the authoritative source for tenant-specific communications
• Microsoft Learn as the home for product documentation and implementation guidance
What you can do to prepare
•
In September, begin using the AI at Work roadmap as
your primary destination for roadmap planning.
• Review internal processes, documentation, bookmarks, and communications that currently reference Release Planner, Release Plans, or release wave announcements.
•
Configure roadmap filters, RSS subscriptions, and CSV exports
to support your organization's planning processes.
•
Evaluate the Release Communications MCP Server
if your organization integrates roadmap data into planning workflows or AI tools.
• Continue using Message Center for tenant-specific change notifications and deployment communications.
Additional information
The AI at Work roadmap provides a single destination for roadmap information across Microsoft
business applications, productivity experiences, Copilot, agents, and AI solutions. Organizations
are encouraged to familiarize themselves with the roadmap's filtering, export, RSS, and MCP
capabilities before September 2026 publishing begins.

items.title: Microsoft Teams: Introducing Facilitator in GCC organizations
items.body:
[What and why]
We are introducing Facilitator in Microsoft Teams meetings for Government Community Cloud (GCC) organizations. Facilitator is an AI-powered meeting assistant that helps participants capture collaborative notes in real time, answer questions about meeting discussions, and keep meetings focused on their agendas and objectives. This experience helps teams spend less time documenting meetings and more time participating in discussions.
[Rollout schedule]
• General Availability (GCC): Rollout will begin in mid-December 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-January 2027.
[Impact on your organization]
Who is affected
• GCC organizations using Microsoft Teams.
• Users with Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses who are enabled to use Facilitator.
Platforms and services
• Microsoft Teams for Windows desktop
• Microsoft Teams for Mac desktop
• Microsoft Teams for the web
• Microsoft Teams Rooms
What will happen
After this rollout, enabled users in GCC will be able to use Facilitator during Microsoft Teams meetings. In-room participants using Teams Rooms will also be able to view Facilitator chat interactions and AI-generated notes.
Licensing requirements
• A Microsoft 365 Copilot license is required to initiate and interact with Facilitator.
Facilitator capabilities
• Automatically generate meeting notes in real time that participants can review and edit together.
• Get AI-generated answers about meeting discussions to clarify information and keep participants aligned.
• Follow meeting agendas, track discussion progress, and help teams focus on their objectives.
Administrator controls
• Administrators can manage Facilitator availability for their organization or specific groups of users through the Teams admin center.
• Facilitator is allowed by default unless your organization blocks the app.
• Facilitator is not automatically activated in meetings; users must enable it.
• Administrators can control access through Teams app management settings.
Security, compliance, and privacy
• Facilitator is built on our approach to enterprise security, compliance, and privacy.
• Microsoft Purview provides capabilities to help organizations discover, protect, and govern supported AI interactions, including auditing, eDiscovery, and data lifecycle management.
• Administrators should review applicable Microsoft Purview capabilities and Facilitator-specific limitations to ensure the experience aligns with their organization's security and compliance requirements.
Known limitations
• AI-generated meeting notes do not automatically inherit sensitivity labels applied to the meeting. For example, if a meeting is labeled Highly Confidential, the AI-generated notes will not automatically receive the same sensitivity label.
• Administrators should consider this limitation when determining which meetings are appropriate for Facilitator and advise users to avoid enabling AI-generated notes for sensitive discussions where automatic label inheritance is required.
[Action required and recommendations]
No administrator action is required for the rollout itself; however, we recommend that you:
• Review Facilitator app availability and determine whether it should be available to all users or specific groups.
• Verify that intended users have the required Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses.
• Review your organization's security and compliance requirements to evaluate how AI-generated meeting notes and interactions align with existing data governance policies.
• Prepare users by communicating Facilitator availability and providing guidance on enabling it during meetings.
[Learn more]
• Data, Privacy, and Security for Microsoft Copilot | Microsoft Learn
• Facilitator in Microsoft Teams meetings | Microsoft Support
• Microsoft Purview data security and compliance protections for Microsoft 365 Copilot and other generative AI apps | Microsoft Learn
• Set up Facilitator in Microsoft Teams - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn
[Compliance considerations]
Does the change store new customer data?
• Yes: Facilitator creates and stores meeting notes, including user prompts and responses. Artifacts are stored in Microsoft 365 services and subject to applicable data governance and retention controls.
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed (e.g., documents, emails, chats, etc.)?
• Yes: Facilitator processes meeting conversations to generate notes, summaries, and responses to participant questions.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?
• Yes: The release introduces Facilitator, a meeting agent, to GCC customers. Which can generate collaborative meeting notes, respond to questions using meeting context. This expands generative AI capabilities that process customer meeting data within the GCC environment.
Does the change provide a new way of communicating between users, tenants, or subscriptions?
• No: Facilitator operates in existing Microsoft Teams meetings and conversations
Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI?
• Yes: Facilitator introduces an AI-powered meeting experience that enables users to interact with generative AI directly within Teams meetings.
Does the change modify, interrupt, or disable any Microsoft Purview capabilities? No, but there are important limitations.
• Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies or enforcement: No change to existing policies.
• Information Protection labels or sensitive information types: AI-generated notes do not automatically inherit meeting sensitivity labels.
• Audit logging capabilities: Facilitator AI interactions are supported by Purview.
• eDiscovery or Content Search: Facilitator interactions and generated notes are support documented discovery mechanisms.
• Retention policies, holds, or deletion workflows: Facilitator interactions and notes require appropriate retention policy configuration.
Does the change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities (e.g., Purview or admin reporting)?
• Yes, new activity to govern: Facilitator introduces new AI-generated content and interactions that administrators may need to monitor and manage. Administrators may need to review existing policies and reporting processes to ensure Facilitator-generated content is appropriately governed.
Does the change modify how users can access, export, delete, or correct their personal data within Microsoft 365 services (GDPR Data Subject Rights)?
• No intended change to existing Data Subject Rights mechanisms.

items.title: (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot: Introducing Federated Copilot connectors in GCC, GCC High, and DoD environments
items.body:
Updated November 11, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.
[What and why]
We're introducing Federated Copilot connectors to Microsoft 365 Copilot for GCC, GCC High, and DoD organizations. Federated Copilot connectors enable organizations to securely connect Microsoft 365 Copilot to supported third-party data sources by using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Copilot retrieves data from the source in real time using the user's identity and permissions, without indexing the external data in Microsoft 365. This gives organizations access to relevant, up-to-date information in their Copilot workflows while providing admins with centralized governance and control.
At general availability, federated Copilot connectors will be supported in the Researcher agent, Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, and Agent Mode in Microsoft Excel.
[Rollout Schedule]
• General Availability (GCC): Rollout begins in late October 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-November 2026.
• General Availability (GCC High): Rollout begins in late October 2026 and is expected to complete by late November 2026.
• General Availability (DoD): Rollout begins in late October 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-December 2026.
[Impact on your organization]
Who is affected
• Organizations in GCC, GCC High, and DoD environments that use Microsoft 365 Copilot.
• Admins responsible for managing Copilot connectors.
• Microsoft 365 Copilot users where an admin has enabled a federated Copilot connector for their organization or designated users.
Platforms and services
• Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat
• Researcher agent
• Agent Mode in Microsoft Excel
• Microsoft 365 admin center
What will happen
• Federated Copilot connectors are off by default. No federated Copilot connector will be available to users until an admin enables it.
• When enabled, a federated Copilot connector can retrieve data from its third-party source in real time by using the user's identity and permissions. External data accessed through federated Copilot connectors is not indexed in Microsoft 365.
• Admins can manage federated Copilot connectors from Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors.
• Admins can view available Microsoft-published federated Copilot connectors and enable or disable individual connectors for their organization.
• Admins can use staged rollout to make a connector available to a limited set of users before broader deployment.
[Action required and recommendations]
No action is required if you don't plan to enable federated Copilot connectors.
If your organization plans to use federated Copilot connectors:
• Review the federated Copilot connectors available in Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors.
• Determine which connectors, if any, are appropriate for your organization.
• Consider using staged rollout to make a connector available to a limited set of users before broader deployment.
• Notify affected Copilot users and update your internal documentation as appropriate.
[Learn more]
We will update this post with new documentation prior to rollout.
[Compliance considerations]
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Microsoft 365 Copilot gains real-time access to data in supported third-party systems through Model Context Protocol (MCP). Access is governed by the user’s identity and permissions in the source system. External data accessed through federated Copilot connectors is not indexed in Microsoft 365.Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI, machine learning, or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Copilot can select tools exposed by a connector’s MCP server at runtime to retrieve information from third-party systems.
